fix.1_save_pin: save/fight.js saveLoadout() writes equip_load_pinned off sim.player.equipLoadPinned; Engine._publishEquipLoad() is its sole writer (mirror() does not touch it); _restoreFightFromSave() restores the pin AND its value instead of clearing it unconditionally. A blob with the field undefined reads false = round-3 behaviour, so no old save is retro-pinned. RULES #7 is honoured because the acceptance re-reads the TIER out of the running world after the load, not the bytes.
fix.2_burden_worn: _recomputeBurden() adds _handWeights() (weapon + shield + talisman) and skips right/left/talisman pack rows, exactly as _recomputeEquipLoad() does. ONE OBJECT ONE WEIGHT: both ratios read the fight's own number.
fix.4_feather_clamp: engine._equipLoadOffset holds the live spell offset; _publishEquipLoad() computes pct = max(0, base + offset) and clamps the SUM, so apply and undo are exact inverses at every magnitude. magic/apply.js loadHandler goes through engine._addEquipLoadOffset. This ALSO deletes the delta-origin state the round-3 verdict §C named as C5's root cause: the producer is now a plain idempotent assignment and needs no construction-site seed.
fix.5_refusal_visible: _sayEquip() puts prose on engine.uiToast() (ui/hud.js E11); the raw diagnostic naming 87 weapon ids stays on the event as ev.refused, the prose is ev.said.

delete_the_fix.which_shape: five independent single fixes, not two-guards-for-one-defect and not inert. Each has its own arm; cutting any one alone returns that one defect and leaves the others fixed. The one place two arms interact is `savepin`+`hands` and that is DELIBERATE and reported as a 2x2: with the hands also blind the sum stays inside LIGHT (20.410959%) and the cliff is never crossed, which is exactly why nobody saw this until round 3 added the hands.
delete_the_fix.all_five_ride_engine._w116Break: verified by grep; none rides `combat.d`, which is the carrier that made round 3's `oversprint` arm inert. Round 3's seven arms are untouched.
delete_the_fix.offline: tools/harness/w1-16-r4-offline.mjs — 6 checks PASS on HEAD, ALL SIX RED under --selftest. The runner exits non-zero if ANY check is still green under --selftest, so an inert arm fails the instrument rather than passing it.
delete_the_fix.live: tools/harness/w1-16-r4-live.mjs — 7 probes, all coupled=true, exit 0. Every probe runs both arms.

two_defects_my_own_probes_found_in_my_ow: THE TALISMAN WAS WEIGHED TWICE. The rod is an inventory row in the `talisman` slot AND the MagicSystem's catalyst, and the first version summed both — the dressed fixture read 55.8 kg for 52.8 kg of objects, i.e. the exact `one object, two weights` defect I had just claimed to make impossible. `_recomputeEquipLoad`/`_recomputeBurden` now skip the `talisman` pack row for the same reason they skip `right`/`left`.

MY FIRST `feather` TEARDOWN WAS INERT. It switched only the magic handler, so the producer's new assignment wiped the offset away and the cut arm showed the spell doing NOTHING (13.013699 -> 13.013699 -> 13.013699) instead of reproducing the defect. An arm has to switch BOTH writers. It now restores round 3's delta-and-clamp producer verbatim and reproduces 13.013699 -> 0 -> 42.833333.

AND ONE IN A CONTROL: the first `overloaded` button-up control ran immediately after the held run, from a body already at speed — 6.208 m with the button UP against 5.277 m with it held, which reads as sprint making you slower. Each walk now gets a fresh dress-and-curse; both are 5.277 m.
